messages:
anna_support: Heads-up: customer (kevin_customer) reporting 502s and huge token counts after region flip. They pinned eu-west-2 but traces show cross-region round-trips and duplicate billing.
maria_oncall: ticket: https://zendesk.example/12345 — customer saw ~3x token billing in a 30m window. they're really unhappy.
devon_infra: Can you paste a minimal repro request and which model/route you hit?
kevin_customer: kevin_customer: here's a curl we used. We set region=eu-west-2 at client but logs show us-west-2 interleaving.
kevin_customer: curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'
anna_support: I pulled their trace spans: routing went eu-west-2 -> us-west-2 -> eu-west-2 within seconds. Looks like the router flipped twice and retried, causing double token accounting.
luis_prodops: That shouldn't happen. Failover should pick fallback and keep affinity. Maybe probe TTL expired and router re-evaluated during the session.
devon_infra: Edge probe logs:
```
2026-02-14T08:04:11Z probe-agent[eu-west-2]: heartbeat OK
2026-02-14T08:06:22Z probe-agent[eu-west-2]: heartbeat TIMEOUT
2026-02-14T08:06:23Z router: failover eu-west-2 -> us-west-2 (session retry)
2026-02-14T08:06:24Z probe-agent[eu-west-2]: heartbeat OK
2026-02-14T08:06:25Z router: re-route us-west-2 -> eu-west-2
```
devon_infra: So a single timeout triggered an immediate failover and then immediate recovery, causing a bounce.
maria_oncall: Sounds like a false negative / probe flap. Could be packet loss or aggressive probe thresholds.
anna_support: Customer says they keep a single persistent TLS connection per session. If router flips mid-connection we spawn new server-side tokens and bill both.
luis_prodops: Billing metrics show token counts spiking in lockstep with routing flips for that org.
sre_bot: @channel auto-alert: multi-region probe flapping detected for eu-west-2 08:06:20-08:06:30 UTC. SREs assigned.
maria_oncall: Mitigation plan (short): raise probe failure_count from 1 -> 3 for eu-west-2 and enable sticky_affinity_hold=120s after failover so we don't bounce instantly.
devon_infra: Risk: this reduces sensitivity to real region outages. We'll stage the change and run smoke tests.
anna_support: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) drop probe packets with iptables for ~5-10s
2) observe router failover
3) restore packets and see router flip-back within 1-2s
So current policy triggers on single probe failure.
luis_prodops: Current router config: failure_count=1, failure_window=5s, immediate_failover=true.
skevin_customer: ETA on fix? Our tenants are getting noisy billing and we're escalating.
maria_oncall: Short-term ETA 30-60m: bump failure_count to 3 and sticky affinity hold to 120s for europe regions. Long-term: investigate probe agent robustness and routing hysteresis.
devon_infra: Patch opened: router-config/patch-2026-02-14-eu-sticky. I'll canary deploy to staging now. Smoke tests:
```
# staging simulate probe loss
sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 9000 -j DROP
sleep 12
sudo iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 9000 -j DROP
# session check
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer STAGE" -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/chat -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```
luis_prodops: Also adding regression detector: if single org token billing >2x within 5m and coincident routing flips, auto-create high-priority ticket and alert billing squad.
maria_oncall: Devon, after deploy please collect probe-agent debug logs and router traces for a 10m window and attach to the incident thread for the postmortem.
devon_infra: Will do. Canary deploy started.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for router-config/patch-2026-02-14-eu-sticky
anna_support: I'll draft a short customer message explaining we're softening failover sensitivity and monitoring for billing regressions. @kevin_customer we can share wording.
kevin_customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick coordinated response.
maria_oncall: Postmortem owner: luis_prodops. Next steps: collect logs, validate canary, roll to prod, monitor 7 days.
luis_prodops: Acknowledged. I'll open the incident doc and link it here when ready.
